en: Our national bird, the Philippine eagle, is so large and powerful that it can hunt monitor lizards and flying foxes by gliding silently through the canopy.
The original copies of the Katipunan's secret magazine, Kalayaan, were printed using a small, manually operated printing press hidden inside a house in Binondo, Manila.
In the Philippine government, the Vice President can be appointed to head a cabinet department while simultaneously remaining the first in line to succeed the President.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over two thousand years ago by carving the mountains entirely by hand without using any modern machines.
Dr. Fe del Mundo, the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School, invented a bamboo incubator to help rural babies survive without electricity.
The carabao, our national animal, has skin with very few sweat glands, which is why it loves to wallow in mud and water to cool down.
Before the Spanish arrived, Filipinos wrote on bamboo using Baybayin, an ancient alphabet where each consonant symbol automatically includes the vowel "a" sound.
The MassKara Festival in Bacolod was originally created in 1980 to lift the city's spirits during a severe economic crisis and a tragic ferry sinking.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polyglot who could speak and write in at least twenty-two different languages, including Latin, Greek, and Japanese.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is historically demonstrated by an entire community of neighbors physically carrying a traditional nipa hut to a new location.
The smallest local government unit in the Philippines, the barangay, gets its name from the balangay, the large wooden boats used by early settlers.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the two-way videophone and discovered a physics principle about electrical resistance that is now officially called the Zara Law.
